title: Activation Cruise Control: rollout playbook scratchpad
body:
PURPOSE
This is a working scratchpad for an operational pattern were calling "Activation Cruise Control" — a lightweight, instrumented canary + A/B framework that treats staged exposure like a PID controller: small adjustments, telemetry-driven, with explicit integrator/derivative checks (trend + burst) rather than only threshold gates.

Scope
- Intended for product features and model routing changes that are latency-sensitive and safety-sensitive (LLM output drift, policy violations, cost spikes).
- Works across hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments; routing adjustments must be API-driven and reversible.

Assumptions
- Per-route telemetry (p50/p95 latency, infra errors, model-health signals) is available with 30s granularity.
- We have blue/green-compatible model variants or weight-based routing to perform soft shifts.
- Synthetic traffic runner exists in CI and can generate deterministic probes matching top 5 customer journeys.

Quick start (90m ops checklist)
1) Pre-flight: confirm canary cohort (seed users or micro-slices) and timing windows with stakeholders. Tag the release in GitHub.
2) Baseline capture: run synthetic probes for 15 minutes to capture pre-change distribution (latency, token usage, top-10 prompts).
3) Launch: route 0.5% traffic -> 3% -> 10% (each step 10-15 minutes unless derivative alerts fire).
4) Observe: run telemetry sweep and manual spot-checks at each step. Call the steward if any adverse signal.
5) Ramp or rollback per decision heuristics below.

Roles & Responsibilities (practical)
- Release Steward (owner): runway decisions, coordinate ops. (usually PM or ENG owner)
- Observability Lead: monitors dashboards, escalates anomalies.
- Model Steward / ML Eng: inspects model outputs for quality drift, runs offline evals.
- SRE (oncall): executes traffic controls, toggles weights, runs hotfixes.
- Customer Success backup: prepared to message customers if exposure is broader.

Decision heuristics (Activation Cruise Control specifics)
- Commitment signals (fast): 2x baseline error-rate spike OR p95 latency +200ms over baseline sustained for 3 consecutive samples (90s).
- Trend signals (integrator): 20% increase in user-reported negative-feedback rate over 30 minutes.
- Derivative signals (burst): any single-sample CPU/GPU saturation >95% or token billing spike >3x expected for that cohort.
- Soft guard: if p50 increases but p95 stable, hold and collect more data; do NOT auto-rollback unless other signals present.

Action matrix (what to do when a signal fires)
- Fast failure (error spike, policy violation): immediate 100% rollback of new variant + page SRE + notify steward.
- Resource saturation: shift 60% of canary traffic to lower-cost model variant or dedicated pool and pause ramp.
- Quality noise (ambiguous): throttle increase (pause ramp, keep at last safe %), run targeted eval set + human review (Model Steward).

Staged exposure plan (example weights)
- Step 0: 0.5% (10m probe window)
- Step 1: 3% (15m)
- Step 2: 10% (30m)
- Step 3: 30% (1h)
- Step 4: 100% (full flip over a rolling 2h window)
Notes: timing flexible based on traffic volume; smaller products can opt for longer windows to increase statistical power.

Slicing guidance (how to pick cohorts)
- Start with synthetic + low-risk internal cohorts (employees, beta users).
- Next wave: geographically mixed random micro-cohorts (e.g., 0.1% of requests per continent) to validate network effects.
- Avoid single-tenant exposure until stable unless customer explicitly requested.

Instrumentation checklist (pre-launch)
- End-to-end provenance on requests (route variant, model version, prompt hash).
- Automated eval harness runs (quality metrics, hallucination surface by prompt set).
- Cost telemetry per-route and per-token; budget alert if estimated spend > X/day (tunable).
- Uptime and capacity alarms surfaced in runbooks.
- Slack alert rules for steward channel and oncall.

Synthetic probe plan
- Probe suite mirrors top 20 user intents, plus edge adversarial prompts.
- Run probes at steady 1qps for canary cohort during each step and compare distributional deltas (token counts, top-k next-token entropy).
- Store probe traces for at least 7 days for retrospective debugging.

Observability dashboard (minimum tiles to watch)
- Latency histogram p50/p95/p99 by route & model variant
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and model-internal failure flags
- Output-quality regression flag (automated eval score delta)
- Cost per 1k tokens and cumulative spend delta vs baseline
- Resource utilization (GPU mem, CPU steal, queue depth)
- Human review sampling queue size and review outcomes

A/B testing notes (when to treat as experiment vs rollout)
- If hypothesis is directional (improve NPS or conversion), set up proper A/B with randomized assignment and power calc before ramp.
- For model behavior changes where safety is priority, prefer staged rollout with asymmetric routing (holdback groups) rather than classic A/B.
- Metric hygiene: define primary metric, guardrail metrics, and sample size. Use Holm-Bonferroni correction where there are multiple simultaneous metrics.

Cost-latency tradeoffs (practical heuristics)
- If p95 latency improves but cost per-token increases >30% and revenue uplift unclear, cap exposure and route a fraction to cheaper variant.
- Introduce cost SLO: daily token spend delta must be < threshold set on product lane. If crossed during ramp, auto-pause.

Communication templates (quick)
- Canary-pass: "Canary stable at 10% after 30m: latency and quality within tolerance. Proceed to 30%. Steward: @name"
- Canary-fail: "Rolling back variant X to vY due to p95 latency spike and increased error rate. See <link to run> for traces. Paging SRE."

Unresolved questions and tradeoffs (notes to discuss)
- How to formalize PID-like controller parameters (proportional gain = percent step size? derivative = burst sensitivity?).
- Should we build a control-loop library in the console for automated modest ramps (with human-in-loop as default)?
- How to manage nested rollouts (multi-model route changes across dependent services) without oscillation?

Next steps (owners & tiny tickets)
- [Evelyn] Draft a minimal runbook template that maps to this pattern (ticket RD-1124).
- [Marco] Add synthetic probe set to CI for release branches (PR open).
- [Aisha] Draft dashboards and put on steward channel.

Appendix: quick JSON payloads for ops (pasteable)
- traffic update (example): {"route":"/chat/v1","variant_weights":{"v1":90,"v2":10}}
- probe request template: {"prompt_hash":"<sha1>","trace_id":"<uuid>","user_type":"probe"}

Notes to self (short)
- Keep ramp conservative when changing decoding params or token limits.
- Prioritize quick-look synthetic probes before relying on noisy production signals.
- Human review loop is the most time-consuming but often catches subtle regression patterns automation misses.

-- end scratchpad --
